strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Execute 8 dependent all-reduce operations sequentially with intermediate local computations (v*s mean, u scaling, additions). Dispatch count is 8 all-reduces. This is the reference approach with no optimization, highest latency due to serial collective dependencies but simplest correctness guarantees.

strategies.name: Pipelined All-Reduce with Overlapped Compute
strategies.desc: Issue all-reduce operations asynchronously and overlap local vector operations (computing v, u patterns, means, scaling) during collective communication. Dispatch count remains 8 all-reduces but uses async dispatch to hide some compute latency. Trades code complexity for potential overlap when hardware supports async collectives.

strategies.name: Fused Buffer Construction Reduce-Scatter/All-Gather
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, computing the local transformation (buf = s + BETA*u*(v*s).mean()) only on owned shards between RS and AG. Dispatch count is 16 operations (8 RS + 8 AG). Reduces computation redundancy across ranks by factor of world_size but doubles collective count.

strategies.name: Blocked Vector All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Partition the 16384-element vector into blocks aligned with u pattern boundaries (blocks of 4 or multiples), perform all-reduce on each block independently through 8 iterations, then reassemble. Dispatch count is 8*num_blocks all-reduces with smaller payloads. Exploits potential parallelism in ring/tree topologies for non-overlapping blocks but increases dispatch overhead.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level All-Reduce
strategies.desc:
Exploit multi-node topology by performing intra-node all-reduce followed by inter-node all-reduce at each of the 8 iterations, leveraging faster intra-node interconnects. Dispatch count is 16 all-reduces (8 intra-node + 8 inter-node). Reduces cross-node bandwidth pressure and latency for the dominant communication cost in multi-node deployments.
